subject: execution and isolation as separate dimensions
scenario: How a task runs and where it runs are different questions, and for eleven versions they shared one field. `worktree` sat in the execution enum next to `inline` and `subagent`, so all three resolver rules that isolate a task returned it as a mode -- and each threw the real mode away. A team that needed its own checkout resolved to `worktree`, and every consumer downstream read a subagent where a team was running. The structure is bypassed by merging them again: putting a place back in the execution enum, or writing an isolation rule inside the execution resolver so it returns a mode. Failure looks like: `worktree` reappears as an execution value. A resolution rule declares no dimension, so nothing checks which axis it is implemented on. team+worktree stops being expressible.
expected_behaviors: The execution enum contains no isolation value, and the isolation enum contains no execution value.
Every resolution rule declares which dimension it answers, and is implemented in that dimension's resolver.
The resolver returns both answers, and neither overrules the other.
team+worktree is written down as a real combination: isolating a team does not stop it being a team.
A task written before the split still reads correctly, because `worktree` is translated rather than rejected.
failure_conditions: `worktree` is added back to the execution enum.
An isolation rule is implemented inside the execution resolver, so isolating a task changes how it runs.
A resolution rule carries no dimension, so it can be implemented on the wrong axis unnoticed.
The isolation default stops being shared-checkout, making every worker pay for a checkout.

checks.description: No place in the execution dimension.
Making every worker pay for a checkout by default is a cost, not a safety property.
Isolation has its own resolver; the rules that isolate a task no longer live in the one that decides how it runs.
The case the split exists for.
The graph can record where a task ran, not only how.
A graph written before the split still reads: worktree becomes subagent in its own checkout rather than a value the enum no longer has.

notes: The behavioural half is in tests/test_execution_resolver.py, which drives the resolver with teams genuinely available and asserts that an overlapping team resolves to team+worktree. Its old name was test_an_overlapping_team_becomes_a_worktree -- the conflation written down as a requirement.
